newsitem.title: INDIA: US balloonist leaves India after entry visa mixup.
newsitem.headline: US balloonist leaves India after entry visa mixup.

text.p: American adventurer Steve Fossett, whose round-the-world balloon journey ended prematurely in India this week, left the country tired and dejected on Thursday after he was denied official entry, a colleague said.

Captain Martin Barnes, who flew Fossett to Delhi in a small Cessna airplane on Wednesday evening from the Hindu holy town of Varanasi, told Reuters the record-breaking but exhausted balloonist was forced to sleep in the transit lounge of Delhi airport after being denied entry.
On Wednesday, a U.S. embassy official said Fossett's visa formalities had been approved by the Indian Home (Interior) Ministry.
Barnes suggested that the orders may not have reached the airport on time.
Fossett had planned to address a news conference in Delhi on Thursday but that had to be cancelled, Barnes said.
"He was tired and dejected, so he took an early morning flight to London," Barnes said, adding that Fossett had been invited to meet U.S. President Bill Clinton next week.
Barnes said Fossett planned to make another round-the-world balloon attempt in January 1998.
"That's because he will need a year to plan the next attempt and the weather is generally good between November and February," Barnes said.
The 52-year-old commodities broker set his balloon down on Monday near a remote village about 120 km (75 miles) northwest of Varanasi in northern India as his fuel began to run low.
His six-day flight, which began in St. Louis in the U.S. state of Missouri, shattered two world records.

Although he fell short of his dream of being the first balloonist to fly nonstop around the world, he broke the endurance record of six days, 16 minutes for a manned balloon flight, set in 1981 by Americans Ben Abruzzo and Troy Bradley.

Fossett, who flew more than 16,000 km (10,000 miles), also broke his own record for balloon distance travel when he passed 8,747 km (5,435 miles) over Algeria. He set the earlier mark on a flight from South Korea to Canada.

Fossett's support team, which accompanied him in a small plane, had said the adventurer wanted to hold a news conference in New Delhi after having his $300,000 balloon pulled from a tree where it had snagged.
